Subject: Private GPU Pool: staged autoscale & throughput safety plan

Team / Sam,

Following our workshop last week, Horizon wants a concise staged autoscale plan for their private VPC pool that hits the following:
- Sustained throughput target: 120k tokens/minute for peak tenant loads (p95)
- Warm burst headroom: +50% for predictable marketing/analysis windows
- Failover latency ceiling: 250ms p95 for single-region loss scenarios

What I need from infra/ops + product: 1) a conservative capacity runway (months of safe ops) if usage grows 30% month-over-month, 2) network egress and TCP connection limits we should test, and 3) a graceful degradation plan that prioritizes inference availability over non-essential batch jobs.

I've attached a draft capacity model (capacity_model_v2.xlsx) and a simplified network topology. Can you each flag any assumptions that look risky? Sam—can Horizon's infra team confirm whether their current VPC NAT gateway limits will throttle connection churn at 100k tokens/minute?

Goal: finalize the staging plan by EOD Tuesday so procurement can align on the reserved capacity ask.

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU Pool: staged autoscale & throughput safety plan

Ben — quick pass from product/runtimes. High-level notes:

1) Throughput math (conservative):
   - Baseline per-GPU sustained throughput (mixed 8/16k seq) ~= 18k tokens/min on our optimized runtime profile for the selected model quant.
   - For 120k tokens/min sustained p95, plan for 8 live GPUs (8 * 18k = 144k) to leave buffer for KV cache misses and short-term serialized spikes.

2) Warm burst headroom:
   - We recommend a small standby pool (2 GPUs hot) + fast spin-up policy for pre-warmed instances using our checkpointed VM images. That yields ~50% immediate headroom without model reload.

3) Network & connection limits:
   - At 120k tokens/min with ~30 token average response, estimate ~4k requests/min (requests per inference session vary). NAT gateway scaling needs to support ~4k concurrent connections; recommend testing to 6k to include retries and function calls.

4) Graceful degradation strategy (proposal):
   - Tier A: live inference (low-latency) — highest priority.
   - Tier B: async batch jobs — throttle/backoff when GPU utilization > 80% for >5 minutes.
   - Tier C: non-critical telemetry export & audits — delayed or dropped under stress.

Assumptions attached in the capacity_model_v2.xlsx (sheet: runtime-assumptions). Marking low-confidence items: model memory estimates for quantized variant and network RTT under cross-az traffic.

I'll run a brief simulation with Vivek's traffic curves and push numbers back by EOD Monday.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Rizzi <sam.rizzi@horizon-analytics.com>

Subject: Re: Private GPU Pool: staged autoscale & throughput safety plan

Ben / Marissa,

Thanks — confirmed a few infra constraints on our side:
- Current NAT gateway per-region limit: 5k new connections/min by default. We can raise this but need an ops window and cost estimate.
- Cross-AZ egress is ~12ms median, 35ms 95th in our staging region (us-west-2).
- We have two spare hosts that can be repurposed for the 2-hot standby suggested, but they require a short maintenance window to install the accelerated drivers.

Procurement note: we prefer a 6 month ramp on reserved capacity with a 20% overprovision credit if we commit up-front; otherwise we need the option for monthly reserved increments.

I'll coordinate the NAT limit increase request if you provide the expected connection profile (Marissa/Vivek outputs). Also attaching our internal runbook for host prep (network_topology_vpc.drawio referenced).

Sam Rizzi
Head of Infrastructure, Horizon Analytics

Date: 2026-11-03T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU Pool: staged autoscale & throughput safety plan

Thanks everyone — consolidating next steps so procurement and engineering have the same picture:

Decisions / Actions:
1) Capacity baseline: assume 8 GPUs live for initial launch (protects to 144k tokens/min) + 2 GPUs hot-standby. Marissa to confirm exact GPU type and runtime quant profile Tuesday AM.
2) NAT gateway: Sam to submit limit increase; target 8k new connections/min as safety buffer. Redwood will provide a 2-day stress test script (Vivek) to validate.
3) Reserved capacity negotiation: Laura will propose a 6-month ramp with a 15% overprovision credit to balance Horizon's preference and Redwood cost. (Laura: please loop procurement thread).
4) Degradation policy: implement Tier A/B/C logic in routing layer; Redwood will add a short-circuit path for Tier A when latency approaches the 250ms p95 ceiling.

Attachments to finalize: capacity_model_v2.xlsx (runtime numbers updated), sla-draft-horizon.pdf (SLA placeholders), network_topology_vpc.drawio (host prep notes).

Sam, pls confirm maintenance window options for host prep and we will schedule the driver install. Marissa/Vivek, please push final simulation numbers by Tuesday EOD. Laura, I'll hand the commercial ask after we lock the final GPU SKU.

Ben

--
